item.title: Solved: Understanding the Differences Between Session.run and Tensor.eval in TensorFlow
item.description:
In TensorFlow, developers often encounter two primary methods for evaluating tensors within a computational graph: Session.run() and Tensor.eval(). But what sets these apart, and how can one effectively utilize them in practical applications?

Exploring the Differences Between Session.run() and Tensor.eval()

When you have a tensor t, calling t.eval() is equivalent to sess.run(t) where sess refers to the current default session. This duality manifests in practical coding examples:

import tensorflow as tf

## Example using Session.run()
sess = tf.Session()
constant_value = tf.constant(5.0)
print(sess.run(constant_value))

## Example using Tensor.eval()
constant_value = tf.constant(5.0)
with tf.Session():
    print(constant_value.eval())

In the second example, the session acts as a context manager, establishing it as the default session for the duration of the with block. Utilizing context managers can lead to cleaner, more concise code, especially in simpler test cases. However, for scripts involving multiple graphs and sessions, explicit calls to Session.run() may be more suitable.

item.title: Top 6 Methods to Solve: What are Logits and the Difference Between Softmax and Softmax Cross Entropy with Logits
item.description:
In the TensorFlow API documentation, the term logits appears frequently, particularly in functions like tf.nn.softmax(logits, name=None). But what exactly are logits? Why is there a distinction made, and what is the difference between tf.nn.softmax and tf.nn.softmax_cross_entropy_with_logits? Let’s delve into these concepts with detailed explanations and practical examples.

What are Logits?

Logits refer to the raw outputs from the final layer of a neural network. These outputs are not constrained to be between 0 and 1, which is a prerequisite for interpreting them as probabilities. When a neural network computes scores (or unnormalized log probabilities) for each class, these scores are referred to as logits.
